verdict: OK to lend in Agra stone processing — pursue inlay and finished-slab units with tight monthly stock-and-debtor discipline; avoid quarry-linked and single-buyer exporters.
title: Agra stone, granite & marble processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Agra's stone units buy blocks and slabs, cut, polish and — the local speciality — inlay them, then sell to builders, exporters and retail.** Cash comes in on delivery to traders and on export bills; cash goes out upfront for blocks, sawing, polishing and skilled karigars. The local press coverage we pulled is thin on numbers [1][2][3], so treat this note as first principles plus peer evidence, and collect from customer the block cost, yield per block and karigar wage bill for every proposal. ## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the finished, inlaid piece, not the raw block — so pricing power belongs to units with design capability and repeat buyers.** Peers show how thin the buffer is: Midwest's 1QFY27 revenue rose 35% YoY but fell 11% QoQ [5], and Aro's June 2026 quarter net sales fell 23.72% YoY to Rs 20.62 crore after a 57.04% fall in March 2026 [6]. Working capital is the real risk: one rated peer ran at around 56% average utilisation of fund-based limits through January-December 2025 [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check the stock-and-debtor cycle against drawing power; if utilisation is running near the sanctioned limit, ask for the ageing of finished stock and the top three buyers.**

## What has changed now
**The state demand signal is positive while the national stone output signal is strong, but bank credit is running well ahead of output.** Uttar Pradesh GST collections grew 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and IIP for NIC 23 rose 11.4% YoY with output up 10.2% Apr-to-date [D]. Against that, bank credit grew 18.2% YoY versus output of 10.2% [D] — money is chasing this trade faster than it is producing. **So price the risk for a slower cycle, not the current one; if a borrower's sales growth outruns his GST turnover, ask for the reconciliation.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue inlay and finished-slab units selling to institutional builders and organised retail, and units with a second product line such as quartz.** Peer evidence supports the finished-product route: Midwest reported granite demand strong domestically and from China [7], and Aro already runs quartz alongside granite [10]. Avoid pure quarry-linked units and single-buyer exporters — one rated peer's ratings were constrained by high geographical concentration in Europe [9], and another's cash flows were flagged as vulnerable to real-estate cyclicality [11]. **If a unit's finished-stock days rise while sales stay flat, ask for the buyer-wise sales register; if two buyers exceed half of sales, seek a personal guarantee and reduce tenor.**
watch: Monthly stock statement and GST return (monthly)
Stock ageing above 90 days or GST turnover below sales -> cut limit and seek fresh stock audit
Utilisation above 90% of sanctioned limit for two months -> freeze enhancement, ask for debtor ageing
Block cost and yield per block (quarterly)
Yield falls or block cost rises without price pass-through -> reprice or exit
Attendance drop or wage bill spike -> site visit and reassess capacity
